newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk right-wing party invited to join coalition.
newsitem.headline: Turk right-wing party invited to join coalition.

text.p: A Turkish right-wing party leader was asked on Wednesday at a three-way meeting with the leaders of the ruling Islamist Welfare Party (RP) and True Path Party (DYP) to join their coalition, Anatolian news agency reported.

"At the three-way meeting, the BBP leader received an official offer to join the government from the leaders of the DYP and RP," Grand Union Party (BBP) leader Muhsin Yazicioglu was reported as telling Anatolian via an aide.
Yazicioglu made the comments after a meeting with Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan and his deputy, Tansu Ciller, leader of the conservative True Path Party at Erbakan's residence.
Yazicioglu was reported as saying his party would consider the offer after "certain problems" within the coalition had been resolved.
"Once those problems have been resolved we will consider this offer," the agency reported him as saying.
The support of six MPs from Yazicioglu's party helped the 11-month-old government to narrowly survive a censure motion in parliament last week.

Ciller made no immediate comment after leaving the three-hour meeting with Erbakan. At her residence later she announced a rise in wheat base prices and commented on foreign affairs, but made no comment on the state of the coalition.
Earlier on Wednesday, she suggested holding early polls to clear political deadlock which has hamstrung the Islamist-led government and badly damaged her pro-Western party.
Ciller's wing of the coalition has been steadily crumbling since the army began pushing Erbakan to crack down on Islamist activism in February.
